text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures were little changed by late in the day on Tuesday with traders saying the market had entered into a consolidation period that should limit prices moves in the days ahead. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.16, down 0.12 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts showed a lack of direction on Tuesday, regaining early losses by the close as minor factors were tossed around in thin volume and players awaited UK manufacturing data. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-00/32, down 1/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures spent a relatively uneventful session following the fortunes of German bond futures to settle slightly higher in a market looking for a fresh impetus after the reversal of recent losses. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.30 up 0.1 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets got back on Italy's political rollercoaster for a while on Tuesday before deciding the government was unlikely to fall this week and cutting the day's losses in half. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.03 down 0.47 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries were off lows in late morning trade. Session lows were touched after Richmond Fed reported regional manufacturing activity wasrobust in March. The Bundesbank was said to be seller of 10-year notes earlier. Fed refrained from open market operations, as expected. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-11/32, down 9/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.11 percent.

JAPAN - Japanese goverment bonds (JGB) futures ended down on long liquidation and profit-taking which emerged in the last half-hour of trade. Investors' buying interest in cash JGBs was still strong, especially at the long-end of yield curve, traders said. Weaker yen and stronger stocks limited JGBs' upside. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.93, down 0.19 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The highlight of the early Eurobond session on Tuesday was British Telecommunications' launch of a $1.0 billion five-year bond, priced to yield 15 basis points over U.S. Treasuries via Merrill Lynch and SBC Warburg. Dealers said more dollar-denominated deals were due. The EIB and SuedwestLB tapped the mark sector. Halifax set a 200 million stg 15-year step-up FRN.
